newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares continue advance, seen pausing.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares continue advance, seen pausing.

text.p: Austria's ATX index of 21 blue chips extended its winning streak on Tuesday, ending at a record closing high for the seventh day, albeit off earlier highs.

Traders said the underlying mood remained bullish amid continuing strong leads from main international bourses, but added the ATX was likely to take a breather over the next few days before staging a new attack on the key 1,400 points mark.
"The basic tendency is positive, but the steep advance is over for the time being," said one. Most market participants expect the index to consolidate at between 1,370 and 1,400 points.

The ATX rose 0.82 points or 0.06 percent to close at 1,391.40, after reaching a new life-high of 1,408.07 points earlier in the day. Among its constituents, 10 winners were matched by 10 decliners, one share was unchanged.

Advancers were led by oil and chemicals group OMV, which surged 53 schillings to a new year-high of 1,677 before profit taking erased some of the gains and the share closed at 1,673, a 3.27 percent gain for the day. Volume was heavy with 223,000 shares changing hands.
Engineering group VA Technologie was also hit by a hefty bout of profit taking, falling 97.50 schillings or 3.82 percent to end the day at 2,456.
On the Austrian futures and options exchange, July ATX futures were down 5.5 points at 1,397.5 on volume of 2,311 contracts.
